sources.title: 2023 integrated annual report: biography and governance table
sources.findings: Page 17 gives birth in Casablanca in 1932, Lausanne polytechnic graduate, initial board appointment 1995.
sources.caution: Read targeted biography/table only. No birth day or graduation year. The 2019–2025 term and family description are historical, not current personal status.

sources.title: Board of directors: Othman Benjelloun
sources.findings: Current chairman and CEO; chair of O Capital Group, RMA and Medi Telecom Orange; founder of BMCE Foundation.
sources.caution: Do not confuse with Brahim Benjelloun-Touimi or attribute other directors biographies to him. Honorary fellowships are not earned degrees.

sources.title: Group history and governance
sources.findings: Current chairman; Lausanne polytechnic graduate; family business expanded through multiple generations; 1967 foundation with wife is distinct from BMCE Foundation.
sources.caution: Corporate promotional judgments not treated as independent assessment. No specific engineering discipline, degree title or graduation year established.

sources.title: Moroccan bank history
sources.findings: Founded 1959, privatized 1995; BOA 35 percent acquired 2008; renamed BMCE BANK OF AFRICA 2015 and BANK OF AFRICA–BMCE Group 2020.
sources.caution: Privatization is not foundation. Rename in 2015 differs from 2020; corporate assets and stakes are not personal holdings.

sources.title: Subsidiary network history and BMCE alliance
sources.findings: Network began in Mali in 1982; 25 February 2008 capital increase gave BMCE 35 percent; 55.77 percent majority in 2010.
sources.caution: No claim Benjelloun founded this network in 1982. Historical 2021 stake is not a current stake. 2011 executive handover differs from 2010 majority control.

sources.title: Foundation background
sources.findings: Foundation founded 1995 under framework set by founder Othman Benjelloun; rural education/environment; September 1998 forum statement.
sources.caution: Institutional account is not an independent measurement of educational outcomes; do not imply he taught or personally built schools.

sources.title: BMCE Foundation chronology
sources.findings: 1998 Medersat.com program launch; first rural schools inaugurated 2000.
sources.caution: Launch and school opening are separate. English index.php page returned verification wall; French page read successfully.

sources.title: 13 April 2026: Mohammed VI Tower inauguration
sources.findings: Tower project carried by O Capital Group; Othman and Dounia Benjelloun named among those welcoming Crown Prince Moulay El Hassan.
sources.caution: Press report establishes attendance; do not call him architect or assume every component commercially opened that day. Only relevant inauguration and reception paragraphs used.
